exercises.title: An invitation
texts:
EINLADUNG
Liebe Emma!
Ich habe Geburtstag und mache eine Party. Ich werde 8! Kommst du auch?
Ich feiere am Samstag um 17:00 Uhr in der Friedrichstraße 11. Du kannst bei mir übernachten.
Sag bitte Bescheid, ob du kommen kannst. Meine Telefonnummer ist 43 87 55 62.
Lotte
Lottes Telefonnummer ist dreiundvierzig siebenundachtzig fünfundfünfzig zweiundsechzig.

pages.title: Celebrating birthdays in the office
texts: Birthdays at a workplace - Every company has its own rules, depending on the company's size. It's best to ask around to see how birthdays are celebrated in the company. Sometimes the birthdays of individual employees within a department or work group are available in a public calendar. You can wish your colleagues a happy birthday. They often bring a treat for everyone, like a cake, which is eaten together during a break.

pages.title: Happy Birthday!
texts:
Birthdays are important in Germany. Adults as well as children celebrate their birthday with family and friends. The person celebrating his or her birthday receives flowers, a cake with candles, and gifts.
If it's your friend's birthday, you should wish them a "Happy Birthday!". You buy a present only for good friends, or if you've been invited to a party. If you don't know what you should get the person, it's okay to ask them if they have a particular wish. Many Germans use the English expression "Happy Birthday!" rather than the German "Herzlichen Glückwunsch zum Geburtstag".

pages.title: Numbers from 11 to 19
texts:
The numbers 11 and 12 are irregular.
From 13, the formation of the numbers is mostly regular. In German, the order of numbers is opposite to that in English. First comes the single digit (e.g. drei, vier, fünf...) and then the ten (zehn):
The numbers 16 and 17 are slightly irregular. The single digits (sechs, sieben) lose their endings.

pages.title: Numbers from 20 to 100
texts:
With numbers over 20, the single digit comes first, and then the multiple of ten. There are two special features to note:
The number eins loses the -s when it is combined with a ten.
There is an und between the single digit and the multiple of ten.

lines: Before going to the police station, Lisa and Nico take Emma to a children’s
birthday party. On the way there, Nico draws Emma a picture with
numbers, and Emma teaches Nico how to count to 12 in German.
Wie ist die Hausnummer, Emma? 38 oder 83?
Ah, ja. Dann sind wir richtig hier.
... sechs, sieben, acht, neun, zehn, elf, zwölf.
Sechs, sieben, acht, neun, zehn, elf, zwölf.
Eine Einladung zum Geburtstag von Charlotte.
Ja, und das hier ist ein Geschenk.
der Buchstabe, die Buchstaben – letter (of the alphabet)

das Geschenk, die Geschenke – gift; present
die Hausnummer, die Hausnummern – street number
